subject: 2000 S Geneva Rd gas-station rezone
comment: Mayor and Council Members: Thank you for your time and willingness to consider my below message in regard to the zoning of 2000 South and Geneva Road. I have been directly working with Davies Design Build as the operating partner for convenience stores, gas stations and QSR food establishments. We currently operate in Utah and Colorado markets. My business as a retail and fuel operator began in 2014 in Panguitch, UT. Prior to 2014, my time was spent managing the operations finance team for an ultra-low-cost carrier airline and was a CPA with Deloitte prior to the airlines. This letter is specific to the environment concern discussed in the Planning Commission meeting held on 10/27/2020. New gas station construction is very differently than construction completed 10+ years ago. Below are some of the methods and equipment we use to ensure environmental compliance, which is synonymous with our success as operators and investors. 1. Underground storage tanks (UST): new installs have multiple options to provide continuous monitoring of an environmental release. This is completed through Interstitial Monitoring, which means the USTs have sensors between the exterior shell of the UST and the fuel holding tank of the UST. These alerts are instant when the sensor is triggered (see page 4-5). 2. Automatic Tank Gauging (ATG - Inventory monitoring): this provides automatic inventory monitoring vs manual sticking the tank (like a dip stick on car oil). This is implemented at all our sites that have USTs. The tank readings flow directly to our IT system and allow us to automatically monitor inventory and identify any variance in fuel gallons (see page 3). 3. Statistical Inventory Reconciliation (SIR): this is a method of statically tracking fuel inventory to monitor if an environmental release may be taking place. The IT system we use in connection with the ATG make this an automated process within our business (see page 6). 4. Electronic Line Leak Detection: This piece of equipment actively tests the fuel lines in the ground on a regular basis. Example: 3 people are pumping on the unleaded line, when the final fueler hangs up the nozzle, the electronic line leak detection will engage and pressurize the line. If pressure is lost there will be an automatic stop to that fuel line that would need to be addressed before that line can pump more fuel. This testing can be completed every time a fueling events is finalized (i.e. after 30 seconds of no fuel flow, the test will begin). 5. Double Walled Flex Fuel Piping: If there is a leak in the main pipe, it is released into the exterior piping and the pressure will push it back to a sump containment. This release would be noted through a sensor that identifies liquid in the sump containment or an A/B inspection. Many older sites may have single walled piping, which could result in a line leak directly into the earth (see page 9). 6. Under dispenser containment (UDC) and sump pump containment will be installed to separate fueling equipment from any direct ground contact, providing an additional layer of environmental protection. 7. A/B Operator Monthly Inspections: This inspection includes evaluation of the entire fueling system and documenting it for the state and internal records. 8. Tank tightness testing & pipe tightness testing: this is required by the state each year, we have a good relationship with our contacts at DEQ and have a great track record of compliance. 9. Vapor recovery at delivery: Deliveries should all have vapor recovery. If we witness a delivery without vapor recovery, we will stop the delivery personnel and request that they implement it. We will then report the event to the company’s dispatch group. The above items are not exhaustive but are part of the core items ensuring that our environmental risks are aligned with our investment risk. The financial risk we expose ourselves to if we are negligent concerning the environment would eliminate any investment benefit and no operator that cares about their patrons, business and investors would allow this to happen.

subject: 2000 S Geneva Rd gas-station rezone
comment: I work for Berkshire Hathaway Commercial Real Estate in Utah. I, along with my business partner (Cassidy Baum, cc'd to this email), represent the sellers and the buyer/developer for the two parcels of land on the Orem/Provo border where 2000 South meets Geneva Road. These properties are being proposed to turn into a gas station. Below is a list of our clients in respect to this email: Seller = The Lloyd Taylor Living Family Trust (the family representatives are Lane Taylor and Cyndy Butler). They own 1.24 acres located at 1981 S Geneva Rd Orem, UT 84058 with the parcel number 19:036:0116 Seller = Donald "Kent" Roberts. He owns .96 acres located at 868 W 2000 S St Orem, UT 84058 with the parcel number 19:036:0053 Buyer/Developer = Davies Design Build / Axley-Way Investments located at 240 N 1200 E, Lehi, UT 84043. In preparation for tonight's city council meeting at 6 PM, my business partner and I gathered signatures from as many people as we could who live/work within 1 mile of the properties. Attached you will see a copy of the petition along with renderings of the proposed gas station. To the left of each signature is a description of where the signers live/work. Please note that we were unable to talk to everyone within the 1-mile radius due to residents/employees not being home/at work or for lack of time to talk to everyone. We were able to collect 204 signatures from those wanting a gas station to be located on the North-East corner of 2000 South and Geneva Road. Those who signed all agree that a gas station on the aforementioned corner would benefit their neighborhood. We look forward to tonight's meeting and feel free to use this petition however you see fit during the meeting. I will be in attendance during the zoom meeting if there are any questions you might have in respect to the petition. (Petition emailed to City Council 11/10/2020)

subject: 2000 S Geneva Rd gas-station rezone
comment: I currently work for Davies Design Build, live in Orem somewhat close to the subject property, and am voter. I am sending this comment as a resident who truly would like a convenience store closer. While it may be hard to believe, I am NOT sending this comment because I am an employee with the applicant. No one has asked me to send this. I personally would enjoy having this gas station mainly because it would be much closer to my home than any other gas station. I am also currently going to school and having this gas station on the subject property would benefit many students due to the large number of them that live on our side of town that do not have a gas station very close to where they live. Lastly, I understand the concerns that others may have about having this gas station, but I do not take in consideration those that do not leave a name or some kind of identification with their comments during your meeting. (Mostly due to the fact that one person could easily spam your inbox with multiple comments against the project from another area or not from Orem). Thank you for listening to my comments and I understand if my job at Davies Design Build minimalizes the things I have said.

subject: North Village District zoning/setbacks
comment: I represent a property owner in the district, and a 75 foot setback from the curb makes developing anything on the corner of 1600 N and 400 W very difficult. When developing adjacent to a street, the setback equal to the height is calculated from across the street. The properties being discussed are currently commercial properties, and there are local property owners, residents of Orem, wanting to invest and redevelop and improve property that is currently covered in asphalt, creating affordable housing. And the current direction of making redevelopment more difficult will prevent existing properties from being redeveloped as the city has envisioned.
